questions.question: The most important and widely celebrated festival of Kerela is _________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Onam:-**

 
 
• It is th**e most popular festival celebrated in the state of Kerala, India.**
 
• It is a** 10-day harvest festival **that usually falls in the month of August or September.
 
• The festival is marked by various cultural events and traditional activities such as boat races, flower decorations, and feasting.
 
• **Onam is celebrated to honor the legendary king Mahabali and to welcome his annual visit to Kerala. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ugadi:**

 
 
• Ugadi is a major festival celebrated in the southern states of India, especially in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.
 
• It marks the beginning of the Hindu lunar calendar and is celebrated on the first day of the month of Chaitra, which usually falls in March or April.
 
• The festival is also known as Yugadi, which means 'the beginning of a new age.'
 
• It symbolizes the start of a new year and the onset of spring.
 
• On this day, people clean and decorate their homes, wear new clothes, prepare special dishes, and offer prayers to the gods.
 
• They also exchange greetings and gifts with friends and family
 
 
• It is a harvest festival celebrated in the state of Assam.
 
 
 
 
 
• Nuakhai 
 
 
• It is an agricultural festival celebrated by the people of Odisha.
 
• It is the greatest harvesting festival of Odisha.
 
• It is observed to welcome the new rice of the season.
 
• Nua means new and Khai means food i.e. Nuakhai's Hindi meaning is 'new food'. 
 
• ‘Nuakhai’ festival is celebrated one day after the Ganesh Chaturthi festival.__
 
• The festival has a big significance for farmers and the agricultural community.
 
 
 
• **Gudi Padwa****​**
 
 
• Gudi Padwa, which is mostly observed in the state of Maharashtra, ushers in the harvest season.
 
• According to the lunisolar Hindu calendar, Maharashtrians celebrate the day as New Year's Day.
 
• Gudi, which refers to Brahma's flag, and Padwa, Padva, or Paddava, which refers to the first day of the moon's bright phase, are the two terms that make up the phrase "Gudi Padwa."

questions.solution:

• **India adopted the inward-looking trade strategy, also known as import substitutio**n, during the first seven Five-Year Plans.
 
• This strategy **aimed to increase domestic production and protect local products from international competition. **
 
• This strategy attempted to replace imports with homegrown production.
 
• The government shielded indigenous industries from foreign competition under this policy.
 
• For instance, businesses will be urged to make vehicles in India rather than importing them from elsewhere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Our industries were unable to compete with the goods produced by more developed economies, therefore the government implemented an import substitution programme.
 
• It is believed that if domestic industries are safeguarded, they will eventually figure out how to compete.
 
• There was a chance that foreign currency would be used to import expensive products if there were no import restrictions.
 
• Because industrialization moves quickly and absorbs unemployed individuals, it assisted in addressing the unemployment issue.
 
• This immediately contributed to economic growth by assisting in the development of a strong industrial base in our nation.

questions.question: The Rashtrakuta king who conquered the Cholas was:
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Krishna III, the Rashtrakuta king, conquered the Cholas in 949 CE.**
 
• He defeated the Chola king Parantaka I and annexed the Chola empire. 
 
• **Krishna III was the last great ruler of the Rashtrakuta dynasty. **
 
• **He ruled from 939–967 CE. **
 
• He also fought against the Chalukyas of Vengi and the Parmaras of Malwa. 
 
• After **defeating the Cholas, Krishna III divided the Chola empire among his slaves. **
 
• **He then built a temple and erected a victory pillar in Rameshwaram. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Rashtrakuta Empire of Manyakheta was founded by Dantidurga (reigned 735-756 CE), also known as Dantivarman II.
 
• Gulbarga was his capital in Karnataka.
 
• He was succeeded by his uncle Krishna I, who extended the kingdom to all of Karnataka.
 
• In 753 Dantidurga defeated the Chalukyas and took the titles Rajadhiraja and Parameshvara.
 
• In the mid-eighth century, Rashtrakuta chief Dantidurga overthrew his Chalukyan overlord and performed a ritual called hiranya-garbha (literally, the golden womb).
 
• It was believed that performing this ritual with the help of Brahmanas would result in the sacrificer being reborn as a Kshatriya, even if he was not a Kshatriya by birth.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct formula for calculating gross primary deficit?

options.text: Gross fiscal deficit − Borrowing from RBI
Gross fiscal deficit + Net interest liabilities
Gross fiscal deficit − Borrowings from abroad
Gross fiscal deficit − Net interest liabilities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross fiscal deficit - Net interest Liabilities**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross Primary Deficit **is the Gross Fiscal Deficit less interest payments.
 
• Net Primary Deficit is **Net Fiscal Deficit minus net interest payments**.
 
• Fiscal deficit indicates total government borrowing requirements including interest whereas primary deficit indicates total government borrowing requirements excluding interest payments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The deficit is the amount by which the spending done in a budget surpasses the earnings. 
 
• There are three types of deficit:

 
• **Revenue deficit**
 
• **Fiscal deficit**
 
• **Primary deficit**. 

 
• Revenue deficit:

 
 
• A revenue deficit refers to the surplus of the government’s revenue expenditure over the revenue receipts.
 
• It reflects the inefficiency of the government to reach its regular or recurring expenditure.
 
• The government may raise its revenue receipts by raising income tax.
 
• **Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure – Revenue receipts**
 
 
 
• Fiscal deficit:
 
 
• A fiscal deficit is the excess of budget expenditure over budget receipts other than borrowings.
 
• It reflects the total government borrowings during a fiscal year.
 
• Gross fiscal deficit = Total expenditure – (Revenue receipts + Non-debt creating capital receipts)
 
• **Gross fiscal deficit = Net borrowing at home + Borrowing from RBI + Borrowing from abroad**
 
 
 
• **​Primary deficit:**
 
 
• The purpose of measuring the primary deficit is to draw attention to current fiscal imbalances
 
• The primary deficit is calculated in order to obtain an estimate of the amount of borrowing that will be required due to current expenditures exceeding revenues.
 
• **Gross primary deficit = Gross fiscal deficit – Net interest liabilities**

• The original Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath features four lions standing back-to-back.
 
• The lions are mounted on a circular abacus, which in turn rests on a bell-shaped lotus.
 
• The State Emblem of India is an adaptation of the Lion Capital of Ashoka.
 
• In the State Emblem, the bell-shaped lotus was omitted, and only the abacus and the four lions were retained.

__
 
• The **Aravalli is a mountain range in India**.
 
• It is the oldest folded mountain range in the country. 
 
• Residual landform, also called Relict Landform, is a landform that was produced as the remains of **an ancient landscape, escaping burial or destruction to remain as part of the present landscape**.
 
• Residual landforms are often the result of changed climatic conditions, but they may be due to volcanism or crustal uplift and down warping.
 
• **Circum-erosional or Relict or Residual mountains (Aravallis in India, the Urals in Russia) are the remnants of old fold mountains derived as a result of denudation (strip of covering).**
 
• Residual mountains may also evolve from plateaus that have been dissected by rivers into hills and valleys.

• Fold mountains

• The depressions from the valleys.
 
• The Himalayas, The Andes, and therefore the Alps are samples of Fold Mountain.
 
• They're the young mountains of the planet.
 
 
 
• Block Mountain
 
 
• When large areas are broken and displaced vertically, Block Mountains are formed. During this case, the uplifted blocks are called horsts.
 
• On the opposite hand, the lowered blocks are called graben.
 
• Examples of Block Mountains are the Rhine Valley and therefore the Vosges mountain in Europe.
 
 
 
• Volcanic Mountains:

• Samples of the Volcanic Mountains are Mt. Kilimanjaro and Mt. Fujiyama.
 
• Andaman and Nicobar islands in India are the tip of the volcanic mountains which rise from the ocean bottom.
 
 
 
• Dome mountains
 
 
• It forms when large globs of magma float up from beneath the crust and push up surface rocks, creating a rounded swelling within the crust.
 
• Once the magma cools, it creates an outsized dome of harder rock under the surface, which erosion sometimes reveals.
